page: Microsoft Azure HB176-24rs_v4 is a memory-dense high-performance computing instance within the HBv4 series. Powered by an x86_64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 24 dedicated virtual central processing units paired with 768 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a high memory-to-core ratio of 32 GB per core. Accelerator hardware is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this configuration.

Storage infrastructure on the instance comprises 4355 GB of local NVMe solid-state storage alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance profile incorporates Remote Direct Memory Access capabilities, facilitating low-latency inter-node communication across clustered environments. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance, requiring standard platform routing configurations for external ingress.

The large memory footprint relative to the dedicated core allocation creates distinct resource density tradeoffs. Workloads with memory capacity demands or extensive memory caching requirements benefit from the 768 GB pool without needing to provision unnecessary compute cores. The substantial local NVMe SSD volume supports heavy scratch file generation and rapid input/output throughput. Suitable workloads include in-memory databases, electronic design automation, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale ETL pipelines, and specialized technical computing applications requiring extensive working memory.
description: Microsoft Azure HB176-24rs_v4 is a high-performance computing server instance featuring 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 768 GB of system memory, providing an extensive 32 GB of RAM per core allocation. Designed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the virtual machine integrates 4355 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes native RDMA capability along with Premium Storage support. The platform contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. With a high ratio of system memory to active compute cores, this configuration trades off parallel core density in favor of memory capacity and fast localized storage. The hardware profile suits high-demand technical computing workloads, in-memory databases, large-scale data transformation workflows, and EDA simulations that require immense temporary storage alongside substantial memory capacity.
